body:
Today the only way to create a task is the small form at the end of a feature on the Features tab (`features.task_form`), which always links the task to that feature and takes only a title. The human wants to add a task of their own from the Tasks tab.

- A **New task** button above the Tasks tab's filters opens a form there: a title, the description in the shared editor (Markdown, with the same formatting tools as the feature form), a project select in a workspace (defaulting to the root's own project; no picker with a single project), and optional feature and milestone selects with "(none)".
- **Create** (disabled while the title is blank) sends `POST {base}/tasks {title, body, request}`, then one `PATCH {base}/tasks/{id}` with the feature and milestone picked, if any, through the same `Link`/`Patched` path the inline row links use. `request` is chosen when the form opens and kept until a create succeeds, so a retry makes one task. One create at a time.
- Each step reports in the form: a refused create keeps the draft ("Couldn't create the task: …"); a refused link says "The task was created without its feature/milestone: …". **Cancel** closes the form.
- On success the form closes and the new task opens below the list as a row click does.
- The feature's own new-task form on the Features tab stays.
- Update the Tasks tab section of the strategy README.

**Tests:** strategy tests for the form (blank title disables Create, request id kept across a refused create, link PATCH sent only when a feature or milestone is picked, form closes and task opens on success); `api.test.mjs` for the POST-then-PATCH sequence.
title: ui: New task on the Tasks tab
